newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: ZAMBIA STOCKS WEEK - LUSAKA RIOTS HALVE VOLUMES.
newsitem.headline: ZAMBIA STOCKS WEEK - LUSAKA RIOTS HALVE VOLUMES.

text.p: Traded volume fell on the Lusaka
stock exchange last week as street vendor riots rocked the
capital on Monday and Wednesday, exchange officials said.
They said volume fell to 234,599 shares valued at 17.27
million kwacha from 481,772 shares valued at 38.46 million
kwacha the previous week.
"Brokers may have found it difficult to keep their business
lines open. Moreover, investors may have found it difficult to
concentrate on investment decisions during the week," exchange
general manager Charles Mate told Reuters.
"The normalisation of business activity in Lusaka at the
close of the week should give a spur to the stock market in the
week ahead," he added.
Chilanga Cement closed at 135 kwacha, up eight kwacha, and
saw 62,000 shares valued at 8.14 million kwacha exchanging
hands.
Farmers House remained steady at 202 kwacha and saw 4,950
shares valued at 999,900 kwacha changing hands.
Rothmans gained one kwacha to close at 71 kwacha on traded
volume of 13,000 shares valued at 923,000 kwacha.
Zambian Breweries closed at 210 kwacha, down 20 kwacha, and
saw 14,756 shares valued at 3.09 million kwacha changing hands.
Zambia Sugar remained steady at 40 kwacha on traded volume
of 125,326 shares valued at 4.88 million kwacha.
Trans Zambezi Industries and Zambia Consolidated Copper
Mines (ZCCM) were untraded during the week.
The index rose by one percent to 241.08 from 238.63.
